strings.list2.title: بازار، پارک اور زرعی فارم
strings.det.unescoNo: یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے کا حصہ نمبر {n}

notes.text: No change. The role file's targets (officialese, stacked participles, calqued word order, filler, Englishisms, over-Arabization, brochure padding) have nothing to bite on in eight labels of two to seven words: none carries a verb, a participle, a filler word or an izafat (P8: every link is the Urdu possessive or «اور»). Each string departs from approved_today only where the owner's decisions require it (DECISIONS «Batch b13-ui»), so an edit here would have to be a correction, and none is owed. Bound and kept: «پارک» not reverted; the two eyebrows byte-identical; nav.leisure = list2.title; «باغات» kept; {n} once in det.unescoNo.

«بازار، پارک اور زرعی فارم» reads as a native heading: three plain nouns with the Urdu comma and «اور» before the last, as the approved label had it. The loan «پارک» is the owner's decision (P16 overridden for this word), so it is not an Englishism for this stage to remove. Kept identical to nav.leisure.

Kept, identical to list2.title. No shorter natural wording within N5 (the bare «فارم» as a list item is refused; «پارکس» is the English plural). The label is shorter than approved_today, so the header can only gain; the measurement is still the coordinator's.

«سیاحتی معلومات» kept. As a section eyebrow it is idiomatic Urdu (the label of an information section, not a person) and sits naturally above both index headings. Weighed against the owner's other candidate «سیر کی رہنمائی»: a phrase rather than a set label, and «رہنمائی» keeps the stem both b12 readers took for a person; stage 1's choice is the safer native label, and the editor sees no fault to correct. The cost stage 1 names ('information' is flatter than 'guide', Arabic «دليل الزيارة») is real and recorded, not acted on.
Byte-identical to list2.eyebrow, as N190 amended requires. Same reasoning.
«پارک اور باغات» kept: a natural category heading (two plural nouns, no verb); the garden word stays as the decision requires.

«بازار اور پارک» kept. COST recorded for stage 4 / the judge, not acted on: the direct plural of «پارک» equals the singular, so the crumb alone could be read 'souqs and a park'; the menu label and «تمام» on the button of the same page carry the plural, as «فارم» does under N5. No wording within the decision removes this («پارکس» is refused).
«تمام بازار اور پارک ←» kept: «تمام» marks both nouns as plural, the natural Urdu button label. The arrow is approved_today's (one space, U+2190).

«یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے کا حصہ نمبر {n}» kept. «حصہ نمبر» before a code is the ordinary Urdu way to number an item, and the phrase before it is the approved det.unesco byte for byte (N2). As a badge line it gives what the English gives: this place is a numbered part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing. Considered and not written: «… میں حصہ نمبر {n}» (mirrors the Arabic «في», but «… میں حصہ» leans towards 'taking part', «حصہ لینا»); «… کا جزو نمبر {n}» (more formal, and parts from det.unesco's «حصہ»); a comma before «نمبر» (splits the badge into a claim and a bare number, against the owner's 'the number WITH a short explanation'). {n} once, at the end, untouched.
